q: A railway servant is promoted to a higher level but does not exercise his option for fixation of pay on promotion within the stipulated period of one month from the date of his promotion. In such a case, his pay is fixed:

options.A: From the date of his next increment in the lower post in all cases
options.B: At the minimum of the higher level in all cases
options.C: Only from the date on which he submits the option in writing thereafter
options.D: In accordance with FR 22(I)(a)(1), that is, with effect from the date of his promotion

q: A railway servant is appointed to hold current charge of the duties of a higher post, in addition to his own duties, during the absence of the regular incumbent. In regard to the duties he discharges in that arrangement, the correct position is that he:

options.A: Draws the full pay of the higher post for the period of the arrangement
options.B: Discharges all the duties of the higher post, including its statutory functions
options.C: Looks after only the day-to-day routine work of the higher post and does not discharge its statutory functions
options.D: Is deemed to have been promoted to the higher post for all purposes

q: A railway servant proceeds on deputation to an ex-cadre post in another organisation. In regard to the pay he will draw during the deputation, the correct position is that:

options.A: He may opt either for the pay of the ex-cadre post or for the pay of his parent cadre post plus deputation (duty) allowance
options.B: He must draw only the pay of the ex-cadre post
options.C: He must draw only the pay of his parent cadre post
options.D: He draws the lower of the pay of the two posts

q: A railway servant returns to his parent cadre on completion of his deputation to an ex-cadre post and his pay has to be refixed in the parent cadre post. That refixation is done:

options.A: At the minimum of the pay level of the parent cadre post, in all cases
options.B: At the pay last drawn by him in the ex-cadre post, in all cases
options.C: Only after deducting the whole of the deputation (duty) allowance drawn by him
options.D: With reference to the pay which he would have drawn in the parent cadre post had he not proceeded on deputation, that is, on a notional basis

q: Promotions to a grade on the Railways are made on a non-selection basis, that is, on the basis of seniority-cum-suitability, and a question arises about the inter-se seniority of the railway servants so promoted in the higher grade. Their inter-se seniority in the higher grade is determined by:

options.A: Their order of position in a merit list prepared by a selection board
options.B: Their inter-se seniority in the lower (feeder) grade
options.C: The dates on which they actually assume charge of the higher post
options.D: Their respective dates of birth

q: A disciplinary authority decides to impose only a minor penalty on a railway servant and issues a memorandum to him proposing that action and calling for his representation. The memorandum for imposition of a minor penalty is issued in Standard Form:

options.A: SF-5
options.B: SF-1
options.C: SF-11
options.D: SF-7

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the defence assistant in a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules:
1. A charged railway servant may take the assistance of another railway servant (serving or retired) or an office bearer of a recognised trade union as his defence assistant.
2. A legal practitioner can be engaged as defence assistant as a matter of right in every departmental inquiry.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A disciplinary authority proposes to punish a railway servant by reducing him to a lower stage in the same time scale of pay for a specified period, with further directions as to whether he will or will not earn increments during the period of reduction. This penalty is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.A: A minor penalty
options.B: Not a penalty at all
options.C: A major penalty
options.D: An administrative measure

q: A senior supervisor in a railway office confines himself to his own work and takes no interest in the conduct of the staff working under him. Under Rule 3(2) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, the specific responsibility cast on every railway servant holding a supervisory post is to:

options.A: Hold a departmental inquiry against any subordinate found wanting in devotion to duty
options.B: Take all possible steps to ensure the integrity and devotion to duty of all railway servants for the time being under his control and authority
options.C: Submit the Annual Immovable Property Returns of his subordinates to the Government
options.D: Report every case of misconduct of a subordinate directly to the Central Vigilance Commission

q: A railway servant wishes to purchase a plot of land in his own name from a person with whom he has official dealings. Under Rule 18 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, he shall not, except with the previous sanction of the prescribed authority, in his own name or in the name of any member of his family:

options.A: Accept any gift on a ceremonial occasion
options.B: Make an investment in Government securities
options.C: Submit his annual immovable property return
options.D: Acquire or dispose of any immovable property by lease, mortgage, purchase, sale or gift

q: An applicant belonging to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category applies for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005. In regard to the application fee payable by him, the correct position is that he is:

options.A: Required to pay double the normal application fee
options.B: Required to pay the application fee in instalments
options.C: Exempt from payment of the application fee
options.D: Required to pay the application fee in full like other applicants

q: A retired railway servant enquires about 'Jeevan Pramaan', which he has been advised to use for his annual life certificate. 'Jeevan Pramaan' is:

options.A: The digital pension payment order issued to a new pensioner
options.B: A biometric-enabled digital life certificate for pensioners
options.C: A health insurance scheme for railway pensioners
options.D: A portal for lodging pension grievances

q: A railway servant dies while in service and his widow claims family pension. Family pension admissible to his family commences from:

options.A: The first day of the month following his death
options.B: The date on which the family applies for it
options.C: The date of issue of the Pension Payment Order
options.D: The day following the date of his death

q: The divorced daughter of a deceased railway servant, who has not remarried and is not earning her livelihood, claims family pension after attaining the age of 25 years. Family pension is payable to an unmarried, widowed or divorced daughter:

options.A: Only up to the age of 25 years
options.B: Only up to the age of 21 years
options.C: Even beyond the age of 25 years, until she gets married or remarried, or starts earning her livelihood
options.D: Only if she was below 25 years of age at the time of the death of the railway servant

q: The permanent post held by a railway servant is abolished and there is no alternative appointment available for him, so he is discharged from service on that account. The pension admissible to him in such a case is:

options.A: Superannuation pension
options.B: Invalid pension
options.C: Compensation pension
options.D: No pension, only service gratuity in all cases

q: A railway servant is declared by the competent medical authority to be incapacitated, by bodily infirmity, permanently for further service and is retired from service on that ground. The pension admissible to him is:

options.A: Compensation pension
options.B: Invalid pension
options.C: Retiring pension
options.D: Family pension

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System retires on superannuation and wishes to withdraw his entire accumulated pension wealth as a lump sum. He is required to utilise the accumulated pension wealth for purchase of an annuity to the extent of at least:

options.A: 20 per cent of the corpus
options.B: 60 per cent of the corpus
options.C: 80 per cent of the corpus
options.D: 40 per cent of the corpus

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System seeks to exit from the system prematurely, before attaining the age of 60 years. He is required to utilise for the purchase of an annuity at least:

options.A: 80 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth
options.B: 40 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth
options.C: 50 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth
options.D: 20 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme retires on superannuation after rendering the minimum qualifying service of 10 years, and the payout worked out for him under the proportionate formula falls below the prescribed floor. The minimum assured payout admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 5,000 per month
options.B: Rs 7,500 per month
options.C: Rs 10,000 per month
options.D: Rs 15,000 per month

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme asks how his assured payout will be protected against inflation after retirement. The assured payout is protected against inflation by:

options.A: Revising the pay matrix every five years
options.B: Granting Dearness Relief on the assured payout, based on the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
options.C: Granting an ad hoc increase of 3 per cent every year
options.D: Linking the payout to the rate of Productivity Linked Bonus

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the Government's contribution of 18.5 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance to the corpus of a subscriber is credited as under:

options.A: 14 per cent to the individual corpus and 4.5 per cent to the pool corpus
options.B: The entire 18.5 per cent to the individual corpus of the subscriber
options.C: 10 per cent to the individual corpus and 8.5 per cent to the pool corpus
options.D: 8.5 per cent to the individual corpus and 10 per cent to the pool corpus

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest to a nearby station within the same locality and the transfer does not involve any change of his residence. The Composite Transfer Grant admissible to him is:

options.A: 80 per cent of the last month's basic pay
options.B: 33 per cent of the last month's basic pay
options.C: 50 per cent of the last month's basic pay
options.D: Not admissible in such a case

q: A railway servant who had drawn House Building Advance earlier in his service for purchasing a flat applies, after fully repaying that advance with interest, for a second House Building Advance for constructing a house. His application is liable to be rejected because House Building Advance is admissible to a railway servant:

options.A: Once in every ten years of his service
options.B: Any number of times, provided the earlier advance has been fully repaid
options.C: Twice during his service, once for purchase of a plot and once for construction
options.D: Only once during the entire period of his service

q: The Accounts Office is working out the cash equivalent of leave salary payable to a railway servant on his retirement against the Leave on Average Pay at his credit and a doubt arises about one component of his emoluments. Which of the following components is NOT taken into account in that computation?

options.A: The pay drawn by him on the date of retirement
options.B: House Rent Allowance
options.C: Dearness Allowance admissible on such pay
options.D: None of the above, as all allowances drawn are reckoned

q: A temporary (refundable) advance sanctioned to a railway servant from the amount at his credit in the Provident Fund is ordinarily recovered from his pay in monthly instalments not exceeding:

A worker in a railway workshop, governed by the Factories Act, 1948, works for more than nine hours in a day and for more than forty-eight hours in that week. In respect of the overtime work so performed, he is entitled to wages at the rate of:

options.A: His ordinary rate of wages only
options.B: One and a half times his ordinary rate of wages
options.C: Three times his ordinary rate of wages
options.D: Twice his ordinary rate of wages

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 26 years of qualifying service, that is, 52 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at retirement are Rs 76,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:

In an accounting year, an establishment governed by the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, has no allocable surplus available. Under Section 10 of that Act, the minimum bonus payable by the employer to his employees for that year is:

options.A: 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year, payable whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in that year
options.B: 5 per cent of the salary or wage earned by the employee during the accounting year
options.C: 8.33 per cent of the net profit of the establishment for the accounting year
options.D: Nil, as bonus is payable only in a year in which the employer has earned a profit

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 92,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate of 30 per cent of the last pay drawn will be:

options.A: Rs 46,000 per month
options.B: Rs 27,600 per month
options.C: Rs 32,200 per month
options.D: Rs 18,400 per month

q: Where the allocable surplus of an establishment in an accounting year exceeds the amount of the minimum bonus payable, the employer shall, under Section 11 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, pay bonus to every employee in proportion to the salary or wage earned by him during the year, subject to a maximum of:

options.A: 8.33 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.B: 10 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.C: 15 per cent of the salary or wage earned
options.D: 20 per cent of the salary or wage earned

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner is Rs 52,000 per month. On his attaining the age of 85 years, the additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 30 per cent of his basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 15,600 per month
options.B: Rs 10,400 per month
options.C: Rs 20,800 per month
options.D: Rs 26,000 per month

q: In a direct recruitment exercise on the Railways, a question arises as to why the reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities and for ex-servicemen is described as 'horizontal reservation'. It is so described because it:

options.A: Is provided separately within the quota of each reserved category
options.B: Applies only to promotions
options.C: Cuts across the vertical categories of reservation, namely Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and the unreserved category
options.D: Can be interchanged with vertical reservation at the discretion of the recruiting authority

q: A railway pensioner surrenders Rs 3,000 per month of his pension for commutation. The commutation value expressed as number of years' purchase for his age on the next birthday is 8.371. The lump sum amount payable to him on commutation will be:

options.A: 30 years
options.B: 35 years
options.C: 38 years
options.D: 40 years

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for 7 hours on a day, the absence being for more than 6 hours but not exceeding 12 hours. options.B: Rs 330

options.D: Rs 770

q: Staff classified as 'Essentially Intermittent' under the Hours of Employment Regulations are rostered for long hours with periods of inaction. The period of rest to which such staff are entitled in a week is not less than:

options.C: 24 consecutive hours including one full night
options.D: 24 consecutive hours, with no condition regarding a full night

options.A: Rs 3,720 per month

options.C: Rs 4,960 per month
options.D: Rs 7,440 per month

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Children Education Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation:

2. Children Education Allowance in respect of a Divyangjan (differently abled) child is reimbursed at double the normal rate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 44,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 22,000 per month. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:

A railway servant retires from service on superannuation on 31st December, and his annual increment in the post held by him falls due on 1st January following, that is, on the very next day after his retirement. For the purpose of computing his pensionary benefits, the correct position is that:

options.A: No benefit of that increment can be given to him for any purpose, as he was not in service on the date of the increment
options.B: The increment can be drawn by him in cash for the month of January after his retirement
options.C: He is entitled to the benefit of that increment notionally, for the purpose of computation of his pensionary benefits
options.D: His date of retirement is deemed to be extended to 1st January so that the increment is actually drawn by him

q: On fixation of pay in the pay matrix under the 7th CPC, the pay of two railway servants who were drawing pay at two different stages in the pre-revised structure gets fixed at one and the same cell of the revised level, so that the senior of the two gets no advantage over his junior. The benefit admissible in such a case of 'bunching' of stages is that:

options.A: One additional increment is granted to the senior railway servant whose pay is bunched with that of his junior at the same cell
options.B: Both the railway servants are granted two additional increments each
options.C: The pay of both the railway servants is reduced to the lower cell of the level
options.D: No benefit of any kind is admissible, as bunching is an accepted consequence of the pay matrix

q: A railway servant whose date of birth is 14th August, 1966 attains the age of superannuation during the month of August, 2026. He will retire from service on:

options.A: The forenoon of 14th August, 2026
options.B: The afternoon of 14th August, 2026
options.C: The afternoon of 14th September, 2026
options.D: The afternoon of 31st August, 2026

q: A railway servant is placed under suspension pending a departmental inquiry and continues to occupy the railway quarter allotted to him at his headquarters. During the period of his suspension, in regard to his leaving the headquarters, the correct position is that he:

options.A: May leave the headquarters freely, as he is not required to attend duty during suspension
options.B: Shall not leave the headquarters without obtaining the previous permission of the authority which placed him under suspension
options.C: May leave the headquarters after merely intimating the Accounts Office in writing
options.D: Shall leave the headquarters immediately and reside elsewhere till the inquiry is completed

q: In a major penalty inquiry, the Inquiring Authority holds some of the charges as not proved, but the disciplinary authority disagrees with those findings and considers the charges to be proved on the evidence on record. Before passing final orders in the case, the disciplinary authority is required to:

options.A: Order a completely fresh inquiry through another Inquiring Authority in every such case
options.B: Impose the penalty straightaway, without communicating anything further to the charged railway servant
options.C: Record its reasons for the disagreement and communicate the findings, together with the report of the Inquiring Authority, to the charged railway servant, giving him an opportunity to make a representation thereon
options.D: Refer the case to the Railway Board for deciding the findings on its behalf

q: An application seeking information is made to the Central Public Information Officer of a railway office, but the information sought is held by, and the subject matter is more closely connected with the functions of, another public authority. In such a case, the application is required to be transferred to that other public authority:

options.A: As soon as practicable, and in any case within five days from the date of receipt of the application, with an intimation to the applicant
options.B: Within thirty days from the date of receipt of the application, without informing the applicant
options.C: Only after obtaining the orders of the Central Information Commission in the matter
options.D: Not at all, as the application must be rejected by the officer who received it

q: In an accounting year, the allocable surplus of an establishment governed by the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 is so large that, even after paying bonus to the employees at the maximum rate of 20 per cent of their salary or wage, a part of the surplus still remains. Under Section 15 of that Act, the remaining surplus is dealt with in the manner that it is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Government at the end of that accounting year itself
options.B: Distributed among the employees as an extra ex-gratia payment in the same year
options.C: Credited to the Staff Benefit Fund of the establishment for that year
options.D: Carried forward as 'set on' for being utilised for payment of bonus in the succeeding accounting years, up to and including the fourth accounting year

q: The services of an employee governed by the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 are terminated by the employer on the ground of an act committed by him which constitutes an offence involving moral turpitude, committed in the course of his employment. In regard to the gratuity otherwise payable to him, the correct position under that Act is that the gratuity:

options.A: Must be paid to him in full in all cases, whatever the ground of termination
options.B: May be forfeited, wholly or partially, by the employer in such a case
options.C: Is automatically converted into a monthly pension payable to his family
options.D: Can be forfeited only with the prior approval of the Railway Board

q: In a railway workshop governed by the Factories Act, 1948, forty-two women workers are ordinarily employed. Under Section 48 of that Act, the facility which the occupier of the workshop is required to provide and maintain for the use of the children of such women workers is:

options.A: A canteen for the women workers within the workshop premises
options.B: A rest room exclusively for the women workers
options.C: A suitable room or rooms, that is, a creche, for the children under the age of six years of such women workers
options.D: A separate first-aid room staffed by a women attendant

q: A child worker is employed in a railway workshop governed by the Factories Act, 1948 and has worked for 240 days in the preceding calendar year. The leave with wages earned by him for the succeeding year, under Section 79 of that Act, is worked out at the rate of:

options.A: One day for every fifteen days of work performed by him in the previous calendar year
options.B: One day for every twenty days of work performed by him in the previous calendar year
options.C: One day for every ten days of work performed by him in the previous calendar year
options.D: One day for every thirty days of work performed by him in the previous calendar year

q: In regard to the manner of payment of wages to staff employed in a railway workshop, governed by Section 6 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the correct position is that the wages are required to be paid:

options.A: Only in the form of goods or other benefits in kind, as may be convenient to the employer
options.B: Partly in cash and partly by way of adjustment against the advances taken by the employee
options.C: Only through a co-operative society nominated by the employer for the purpose
options.D: In current coin or currency notes, or by cheque, or by crediting the wages in the bank account of the employed person

q: A railway workshop governed by the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 ordinarily employs fifteen hundred persons. Under Section 5 of that Act, the wages of the persons employed in the workshop for a wage period are required to be paid:

options.A: Before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage period
options.B: Before the expiry of the tenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.C: Before the expiry of the fifteenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.D: On any day within one month after the last day of the wage period

Under Section 10 of that Act, such a deduction can be made only where:

options.A: The worker has himself admitted the loss in writing before his supervisor

options.C: The worker has been given an opportunity of showing cause against the deduction, in the prescribed manner

q: A railway servant, who has come to know certain confidential information in the course of his official duties, passes on that information to a contractor who is not authorised to receive it. options.A: Shall not, except in the normal course of his duties and in good faith, communicate or allow to be communicated any official information to a person who is not authorised to receive it

options.C: Is required to destroy all official information immediately after his transfer from the post
options.D: May communicate official information to any person on payment of the prescribed fee under the rules

q: A railway servant is placed under suspension and, before his suspension, he was drawing House Rent Allowance at the rate admissible at his headquarters, no railway accommodation having been allotted to him. In regard to House Rent Allowance during the period of his suspension, the correct position is that:

options.A: House Rent Allowance is not admissible at all during the period of suspension
options.B: House Rent Allowance is admissible only at one-half of the rate drawn before suspension
options.C: House Rent Allowance is admissible only if the suspension is revoked within three months
options.D: House Rent Allowance continues to be admissible to him during suspension, at the rate at which it was drawn before suspension, subject to the prescribed conditions

q: A railway servant already owns a house constructed by him at his place of posting and now applies for House Building Advance for putting up an additional portion by way of extension of that very house. options.A: Is admissible to him for extension of his existing house, subject to the prescribed ceiling and other conditions
options.B: Is admissible only for construction of an entirely new house on a separate plot

options.A: Can be granted to him freely, as the date of his retirement has no bearing on the grant
